method: YouTube search (type=video, videoDuration=short, order=viewCount, publishedAfter 2026-10-20) for 4 query families, then videos?part=statistics. About 60 Shorts.
findings: Construction/'how is it built' Shorts are far ahead: bridges and dams 300k-2.5M views (e.g. 'How You Accidentally Build A Thousand Year old Bridge' 2.49M, 'How Are Bridges Built?' Telugu 2.46M, 'How Humans Invented the Perfect Bridge' 2.35M, glass-bottom bridge 3D 2.07M, 'How Dams Work' Telugu 1.92M, Anshun covered bridge 1.74M).

Many top results are in Hindi/Telugu/Tamil/other Indian languages and about Indian structures: Howrah Bridge 832k (Hindi), Pamban + Chenab bridges 810k, Havelock bridge 683k, Polavaram dam 354k, Kallanai (Grand Anicut) 2000-year dam 336k (Tamil), Bogibeel bridge 417k.
Best English example found: 'The Skyscraper Built on a Loophole' (Vancouver House) 644k views, 361 comments.
English 'invention history' Shorts do much smaller: escalator 41k, Otis elevator 26k, soda tab 26k, most 1k-10k. 'Real reason X exists' history facts mostly 1-2k.
Titles that work: 'How was X built', 'How do you build a bridge across a cliff?', impossible-feeling claims (no pillars, no cement, 2000 years old), emoji like 😱, 3D animation.
Satisfying tiny-world/ants animations did poorly (30-96 views).
Caveat: sample is search results sorted by views, so it shows what can reach big numbers, not an average; some big channels may be older/popular channels.
candidate_topics_to_verify_before_use: How the Howrah Bridge was built (cantilever over the Hooghly, no piers in the river, opened 1943)
